bug_description.original: Crash Type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1. Crash State: parse_complex_format -> fuzz_complex_parser.c -> LLVMFuzzerRunDriver. Sanitizer: address (ASAN).
bug_description.normalized: Stage 01 reproduced AddressSanitizer's 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read on the exact staged 110-byte witness with SHA-256 `70b0e482bfca8859b12f4c714c4e4b2fa262286291c07215e476ecc340193887`. The witness begins with `Fuzz` and contains its first embedded NUL at offset 57, so `parse_complex_format()` materializes `length == 57` even though the heap buffer allocated by the harness is 111 bytes (`malloc(size + 1)`). On the staged x86_64 build, `char` is signed, so only 15 of those first 57 bytes satisfy `input[i] > 0x20`; this makes `sum == 15` and selects the `sum < 20` path. The vulnerable call passes the full string length into `read_key_figures(input, length)`, even though that helper later doubles the parameter. `read_key_figures()` only rejects values below 10, doubles 57 to 114, and forwards that as `idx` into `get_the_right_character()`. That helper merely checks `strlen(input) < 40`, so it still dereferences `input[114]`, which is 3 bytes past the 111-byte heap allocation. The patch fixes the exact obligation by changing the call to `read_key_figures(input, length/2)`, so the helper doubles 28 back to 56 instead of 114 and keeps the read in bounds for the reproduced witness.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that materializes vulnerability-relevant state from the fuzzed bytes. It converts the attacker-controlled string contents into `length`, which later drives the oversized helper argument and resulting out-of-bounds index.
source.value_from: The harness copies the exact 110-byte `poc` file into heap buffer `ns`, appends a trailing `\0`, and passes `ns` to `parse_complex_format()`. Because the witness itself already contains an embedded NUL at offset 57, this `strlen(input)` call returns 57 on the reproduced crash path.

relation.description: Source identity relation for the vulnerability-relevant value.

sink.description: ASan crash site. `get_the_right_character()` dereferences the doubled attacker-derived index after only checking that the string length is at least 40, not that `idx` fits inside the string or the heap allocation.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow` with `READ of size 1` at `char_lib.c:58:14` in `get_the_right_character`, and says the faulting address is 3 bytes to the right of the 111-byte region allocated in `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.

root_cause.description: The caller passes the full string length into helper parameter `half_length`, even though `read_key_figures()` later doubles that value before indexing the same buffer. That mismatched helper contract seeds the oversized index that reaches the sink.
root_cause.note: The patch changes this exact statement to `read_key_figures(input, length/2)`, restoring the implicit precondition that the helper argument already be half-sized before the internal doubling step.

parser_admitted.description: For the exact witness, the prefix checks accept `Fuzz` and the signed-char count loop produces `sum == 15`, so `parse_complex_format()` reaches the `read_key_figures` call instead of returning early or taking the `sum > 40` branch.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant tainted scalar is the string length derived from attacker-controlled bytes. For the exact witness, the first embedded NUL at offset 57 makes `length == 57`, and that value later becomes the doubled out-of-bounds index.

fine_trace.note: Source. The first project-code read of the fuzzed string computes `length == 57` from the witness's first embedded NUL at offset 57, even though the staged file itself is 110 bytes long.
The exact witness begins with `Fuzz`, so all four prefix rejection guards fall through and execution reaches the character-count loop.

On the staged build, `char` is signed, so bytes `>= 0x80` compare negative and do not increment `sum`. Among the first 57 bytes, only 15 characters satisfy `input[i] > 0x20`, so this loop materializes `sum == 15`.
Because step 3 produced `sum == 15`, `parse_complex_format()` selects the `read_key_figures` arm instead of returning `-1` or entering the `sum > 40` magic-value path.

Root cause. The caller passes the full string length 57 into parameter `half_length`. Because the callee later doubles that value before indexing the same buffer, this call mis-sizes the helper input by a factor of two.

The helper's only present guard is a lower-bound check. With `half_length == 57`, execution proceeds, and there is no matching upper-bound check that `2 * half_length` still fits within `strlen(input)`.
The helper doubles the tainted value from 57 to 114 and forwards that doubled value as the `idx` argument to `get_the_right_character()`.

The sink helper recomputes the string extent and only proves that at least 40 characters exist. For the exact witness `strlen(input)` is still 57, so this guard falls through without checking the actual safety condition `idx < 57`.

Sink. The helper dereferences `input[114]`. Stage 01's ASan trace shows the harness allocated a 111-byte region with `malloc(size + 1)`, so index 114 is 3 bytes past that heap buffer and causes the reported 1-byte out-of-bounds read.

sanitizer_ground_truth.crash_summary: AddressSanitizer reports a 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow READ in `get_the_right_character` at `char_lib.c:58`, with stack `get_the_right_character -> read_key_figures -> parse_complex_format -> LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput`.
sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves_note: The patch changes `read_key_figures(input, length)` to `read_key_figures(input, length/2)`. For the reproduced witness `length == 57`, the helper then doubles 28 back to 56 instead of 114, so the `input[idx]` read stays inside the 111-byte `malloc(size + 1)` heap buffer.

format.contract: Exact 110-byte file with SHA-256 `70b0e482bfca8859b12f4c714c4e4b2fa262286291c07215e476ecc340193887`: bytes 0..3 are ASCII `Fuzz`, the first embedded NUL is at offset 57, and on the staged signed-char build the first 57 bytes contribute `sum == 15`, so `parse_complex_format()` takes the `sum < 20` arm, passes `length == 57` into `read_key_figures()`, and the helper doubles that value to `idx == 114` before the sink read.
